quis: quī, quae, quod — who (rel., dat./abl. pl., old form = quibus); also quis, who? (interrog.) · also indefinite quis, anyone (after nē/neu, m. nom. sg.); quis locus, which place? (interrog. adj.) · also indef. after sī, anyone (m. nom. sg.: sī quis) · also indef. after quam (m. nom. sg.: quam quis, until anyone) · also indef. after rel. quae (m. nom. sg.: quae quis, whatever any man)
quo: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., m./n. abl. sg.); quō (adv.), where to · also indef. after nē, any (abl. sg.: nē quō nūmine) · also quō, to what end? why? (quō molem … statuēre?) · also quō (conj.), in order that (quō … averteret)
quod: quī, quae, quod — which (rel., n. nom./acc. sg.); quod (conj.), because, that · also interrog. adj., what? (n. nom./acc. sg.: quod genus) · also acc. of respect, wherefore (quod tē per superōs … ōrō) · also indef. adj. after sī, any (n. nom. sg.: sī quod nūmen) · also connective, but, now (quod sī, 'but if'; n. acc. sg. as conj.)
quoniam: quoniam (conj.) — since, seeing that, because, whereas
quoque: quoque (adv.) — also, too (follows the word it stresses) · also quō (adv.), where + -que 'and' (quoque ostendit se, and where she shows herself)
rabies: rabiēs, -ēī (f.) — rage, frenzy, raving hunger (nom. sg.)
rami: rāmus, -ī (m.) — branch, bough (nom. pl.; also gen. sg.)
rebus: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (abl./dat. pl.)
referunt: referō, -ferre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, carry back, bear back (3rd pl. pres.)
regebat: regō, -ere, rēxī, rēctum — to rule, govern (3rd sg. imperf.)
reges: rēx, rēgis (m.) — king (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl. (qui reges)
regia: rēgius, -a, -um — royal, queenly (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also rēgia, -ae (f.), palace, royal house (nom. sg.: rēgia Pīcī)
religio: religiō, -ōnis (f.) — sacred obligation, rite, scruple, awe (nom. sg.)
reliquias: reliquiae, -ārum (f. pl.) — remains, remnants, survivors (acc. pl.)
rettulit: referō, -ferre, rettulī, relātum — to bring back, carry back, revive, tell (3rd sg. perf.)
robore: rōbur, rōboris (n.) — oak; hard timber (abl. sg.)
romani: Rōmānus, -a, -um — Roman, of Rome (m. gen. sg., with rēgis)
romulus: Rōmulus, -ī (m.) — Romulus, founder of Rome (nom. sg.)
ruit: ruō, -ere, ruī, rutum — to rush, hurry, fall headlong (3rd sg. pres.)
rupe: rūpēs, rūpis (f.) — cliff, crag, rock (abl. sg.)
sacri: sacer, sacra, sacrum — holy, sacred; accursed (m./n. gen. sg.; m. nom. pl.)
saepius: saepe (adv.) — often; saepius (compar.), more often, oftener
sanctum: sānctus, -a, -um — holy, sacred, inviolable (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
saturnia: Sāturnius, -a, -um — of Saturn; Sāturnia, daughter of Saturn, Juno (f. nom. sg.)
se: suī (reflexive pron.) — himself, herself, itself, themselves (acc.; also abl. sē)
secus: secus (adv.) — otherwise; haud secus, not otherwise, just so
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedem: sēdēs, -is (f.) — seat, abode, dwelling place, site (acc. sg.)
sedes: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc./nom. pl.) · also nom. sg. (sēdēs fundātur)
sensit: sentiō, sentīre, sēnsī, sēnsum — to feel, perceive, notice (3rd sg. perf.)
sequentem: sequor, -ī, secūtus sum — to follow, pursue (dep.) (pres. part., m./f. acc. sg.)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
similis: similis, -e — like, similar (+ gen./dat.) (m./f. nom. sg.; f. acc. pl. in -is)
singula: singulī, -ae, -a — one by one, each (n. acc. pl.)
soporem: sopor, sopōris (m.) — deep sleep, slumber (acc. sg.)
stare: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm, stand still (pres. inf.)
stratisque: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, strew; slay (perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl.) + -que 'and' · also strātum, -ī (n.) — couch, bed (n. abl. pl.: strātīs relictīs) + -que, and
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subibant: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go under, go up to, approach, climb (3rd pl. impf.)
subiit: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go under, come up; of thoughts, to come to mind (3rd sg. perf.)
successit: succēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to come up to, enter, follow (+ dat.) (3rd sg. perf.)
superesse: supersum, -esse, -fuī — to be left over, remain, survive (pres. inf.)
supplex: supplex, supplicis — suppliant, begging humbly (nom. sg.)
talibus: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (abl./dat. pl.)
tecti: tectum, -ī (n.) — roof, house (gen. sg.) · also tectus, -a, -um — sheltered, covered; tegō perf. pass. part. (m. nom. pl.: tectī silvīs)
tellurem: tellūs, tellūris (f.) — earth, ground; Tellus, Earth as goddess (acc. sg.)
tenebant: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, occupy (3rd pl. impf.)
tenebat: teneō, -ēre, tenuī, tentum — to hold, keep, grasp (3rd sg. impf.)
thalamoque: thalamus, -ī (m.) — bedchamber; marriage-bed, wedlock (abl./dat. sg.) + -que, and
thybrim: Thybris, -idis (m.) — the Tiber (acc. sg., Greek form in -im)
thybris: Thybris, -is (m.) — the Tiber, river of Latium and Rome (nom. sg.; Greek-derived form)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
tuae: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (f. nom. pl.; f. gen./dat. sg.)
tuis: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m./n. abl./dat. pl.) · also f. abl./dat. pl. (tuīs querēlīs)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tuos: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (m. acc. pl.)
ullum: ullus, -a, -um — any (n. nom./acc. sg.; also m. acc. sg.)
ursae: ursa, -ae (f.) — she-bear (gen. sg.; also dat. sg., nom. pl.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how
valent: valeō, -ēre, -uī — to be strong, be able, avail (3rd pl. pres.)
varioque: varius, -a, -um — varied, changing, shifting, fickle (m./n. abl. sg., with aestū) + -que 'and'
venere: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (3 pl. perf., = vēnērunt)
veni: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come, arrive (1st sg. perf.)
venio: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (1st sg. pres.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
ventum: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (perf. pass. part., n. sg., in impersonal ventum est, they came) · also ventus, -ī (m.) — wind (acc. sg.: in ventum, 'into the wind')
venus: Venus, Veneris (f.) — Venus, goddess of love, mother of Aeneas (nom. sg.)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
verum: vērum (conj.) — but, but yet (adverbial n. acc. sg. of vērus)
veterumque: vetus, -eris — old, ancient; veterēs, forefathers, ancestors (m. gen. pl.) + -que, and
videbant: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, perceive (3rd pl. impf.)
vides: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (2nd sg. pres.)
vidisse: videō, -ēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (perf. inf.)
viribus: vīs, vīs (f.) — force, strength; pl. vīrēs, vīrium, strength (abl./dat. pl.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vocari: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon, name (pres. pass. inf.)
volcanum: Volcānus, -ī (m.) — Vulcan, god of fire; fire (by metonymy) (acc. sg.)
